key_insight: Entropy estimation in multi-qutrit systems shifts from variational quantum methods for small systems to CNN-based estimators that scale better and remain robust for larger systems.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a practical workflow for qutrit entropy estimation: use hardware-efficient VQAs when the system is small, and switch to measurement-based CNNs when scalability and noise tolerance matter.
method: Evaluated 11 SU(3)-inspired hardware-efficient VQA ansatzes on ideal simulators for up to three qutrits.
Trained a CNN on tensor-product mutually unbiased basis measurements for two to five qutrits.
Compared performance under varying parameter counts, entangling-gate depth, shot noise, and out-of-distribution states.
evidence_signal: The CNN reached about 0.13–0.16 nats at the 90th-percentile absolute error for four- and five-qutrit systems using only 12.5% of tomography measurements, and performance improved with system size.
watch_item: Results are based on noise-free simulation for the VQA study, so real-device hardware noise and calibration effects may reduce performance.
paper_title: Entropy Estimation in Multi-Qutrit Systems via Variational and Classical Neural Networks
